scope: All priority items, all figures appended to ranked items after the GHE DALY part, country source_url identity, source_url resolution. GHE DALY rank/rate text on ranked items was out of scope (verified earlier).
freshness_notes: Hypertension: GHO series used (2019) is the latest in the GHO API, but the WHO 2025 hypertension country profiles give 2024 estimates (prevalence / control: ARM 51/10, BWA 41/20, DOM 50/23, IND 30/17, JAM 49/21, UGA 28/9). Not changed.
Philippines HIV: 2025 values exist (34,000 new infections, 41% on ART). Claim for 2024 is correct. Not changed.
Zimbabwe malaria: 2024 estimate (148,833) is a 77% drop from 2023 (635,589). Correct as stated.

claims.claim: About 58,000 snakebite deaths per year (1.2 million from 2000 to 2019) (Million Death Study, reported by WHO)
claims.evidence: WHO 10 Jul 2020: '1.2 million snakebite deaths (representing an average of 58,000 per year) from 2000 to 2019'

claims.claim: mostly rural, half in the June to September monsoon
claims.evidence: Source says only 'low altitude agricultural areas' (70% of deaths in 8 states, 2001 to 2014) and 'particularly during the rainy season'. It gives no share for the monsoon and no June to September months ('nearly half' in the source refers to victims aged 30 to 69).
claims.corrected: About 58,000 snakebite deaths per year (1.2 million from 2000 to 2019), mostly in low-lying farming areas and during the rainy season (Million Death Study, reported by WHO)

claims.claim: Newborn screening of 66,833 babies found sickle cell syndromes in 407 (about 1 in 164 births) and sickle cell trait in 9.8% (Serjeant et al., J Community Genet 2017, with the Ministry of Health)
claims.evidence: PubMed abstract: 'screened 66,833 samples with the sickle cell trait in 9.8 %'; 'Sickle cell syndromes occurred in 407 babies'; 66,833/407 = 164; J Community Genet 2017;8(1); co-authors from Southern Regional Health Authority, Ministry of Health

claims.claim: National survey of 97,631 infants found sickle cell trait in 13.3% and sickle cell disease in 0.7%, up to 1.5% in East Central region (Uganda Sickle Surveillance Study, with the Ministry of Health)
claims.evidence: All numbers match the Lancet Glob Health 2016 abstract (97,631 results; trait 13.3%; disease 0.7%; East Central 1.5%; Ministry of Health co-author). Imprecise: samples were from HIV-exposed infants in the Early Infant Diagnosis programme, not a general infant survey.
claims.corrected: National survey of 97,631 HIV-exposed infants found sickle cell trait in 13.3% and sickle cell disease in 0.7%, up to 1.5% in East Central region (Uganda Sickle Surveillance Study, with the Ministry of Health)

claims.claim: US3 measured 0.7% disease prevalence; the study background notes an older, commonly cited figure of 20,000 babies per year born with sickle cell disease that lacked accurate data.
claims.evidence: Abstract: 'In Uganda, 20,000 babies per year are thought to be born with sickle cell disease, but accurate data are not available.'
